newsitem.title: USA: Alleged Thai drug baron arraigned in New York.
newsitem.headline: Alleged Thai drug baron arraigned in New York.

text.p: An alleged Thai middleman linked to one of the largest heroin seizures in U.S. history was arraigned on Monday two days after being extradited from his homeland.
The suspect, Li Yun-chung, 44, was denied bail after he pleaded not guilty during the hearing at Brooklyn Federal Court. He is awaiting trial on a drug-trafficking indictment.
If found guilty he faces life in prison. No trial date was set.
According to federal prosecutors, Li was responsible for importing a 1,070-pound (486-kg) shipment of heroin in 1991, with a street value of $1 billion.

The drugs from the "Golden Triangle" of Laos, Thailand and Burma were seized by Customs agents in Oakland, Calif., during a routine customs check. It is believed that the shipment was on its way to New York.
Investigators in California arrested four men, including Li's brother, Li Yun-hsing. They were all convicted.
Based on a warrant issued from Brooklyn, Thai police arrested Li and he served seven months in jail while fighting extradition. However a judge in Thailand granted Li bail and he fled to Burma.
That release is under investigation in Thailand amid allegations of judicial corruption.
Burmese authorities turned Li over to a visiting Thai diplomat who returned him to Thailand. Li waived extradition and he was brought to Brooklyn on Saturday.
Law-enforcement sources say Li agreed to extradition because rival dealers may have been looking for him, afraid he might spill details of the payoff that got him out of jail.
A co-defendant, Cha Chung-chang, 42, is in jail in Thailand as he fights extradition to the United States. A third defendant, Chao Chou-lou, is a fugitive.

One source close to the investigation described Li as a "prolific middleman." Li allegedly works with Chang Chi-fu, also known as Kuhn Sa, who has been identified as one of the top heroin dealers in the world.
